&api-questions;
The nbfx Status API defines the JavaFX status bar element SPI (StatusElement), the StatusAlignment enum, the StatusMessageService contract for the transient status line, the StatusElementRegistry/StatusElementSpec/StatusElementEntry discovery and loading contract, and the @StatusRegistration annotation with its processor.
A module implements StatusElement and declares it with @StatusRegistration. The processor writes the id, alignment and position to NbFx/Status/<id>.instance; StatusElementRegistry reads the class-based entries through LayerInstances and returns StatusElementSpec values. platform.status is the T0 renderer and owns the themed status bar.
A module contributes the caret, line-separator, project, progress, VCS or application-specific status element with API/SPI imports only; the shell composes the registered elements and initializes each one with its lookup before creating the node.
StatusElementRegistryTest covers the layer metadata, ordering and additional elements. StatusRegistrationProcessorTest covers the generated fragment and the rejection of a class that does not implement StatusElement. The API is under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.
A JDK is required to compile the annotation processor, and a JavaFX runtime is required for StatusElement and the themed status bar.
Only org.netbeans.api.nbfx.status is public. The processor implementation is an implementation detail and is not exported.
The processor is discovered by the compiler through the META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor service, generated by @ServiceProvider(service=Processor.class). StatusElementRegistry reads NbFx/Status through LayerInstances.
This module registers its annotation processor with @ServiceProvider; the status bar renderer is a T0 service in platform.status.
Yes. The processor creates NbFx/Status/<id>.instance entries.
StatusElementRegistry reads NbFx/Status through LayerInstances; discovery creates the registered elements.
None.
The annotation processor runs in the compiler's processing rounds and is stateless. The registry reads the layer and initializes elements on the calling thread; the element's getNode() and the status bar must run on the JavaFX Application Thread.
No code runs on startup beyond the status bar's on-demand discovery; the module contributes a compiled annotation processor and the reader.
No code runs on exit.
No special requirements.
